title: Which job should your first AI employee do?

slides.label: AI employees
slides.title: Which job should AI take first?
slides.body: 5 signs a task is ready. Comment TECH for the template.

slides.label: Sign 1 · It repeats
slides.title: It happens every week.
slides.body: If you only do it twice a year, it isn't worth building for.

slides.label: Sign 2 · Same steps
slides.title: The steps rarely change.
slides.body: If you can write them on one page, an AI employee can follow them.

slides.label: Sign 3 · Clear inputs
slides.title: It starts from something written.
slides.body: An email, a form, a spreadsheet row. Not a hallway conversation.

slides.label: Sign 4 · Easy to check
slides.title: A mistake is easy to catch.
slides.body: Drafts and summaries are safe to start with. Payments and contracts are not.
slides.you: A person approves anything that sends, pays or publishes.

slides.label: Sign 5 · Nobody wants it
slides.title: Your team dreads it.
slides.body: That's where the time and the goodwill come back first.

Which job should your first AI employee do? Comment TECH and we'll DM you the one-page template we use to design every AI employee.

Look for a task with all 5 signs:
1. It repeats every week
2. The steps rarely change
3. It starts from something written: an email, a form, a spreadsheet row

5. Your team dreads it

Start there. Keep a person approving anything that sends, pays or publishes, and add the next job once the first one runs clean.
